drafted_from: tool row in tools/connected-drives/tool-rows.json, read-data/drives.mjs and test/drives.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "List the files in the DCIM folder on my SAMPLE DRIVE, folders first, 200 at a time." It runs tool:list-a-drive-folder with path /Volumes/SAMPLE DRIVE/DCIM and hands back each entry with its kind, size and date.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads the drives this computer shows and changes nothing.
instructions: 1. Run tool:list-connected-drives to get the mount of the drive, for example /Volumes/SAMPLE DRIVE.
2. Say "List the files in /Volumes/SAMPLE DRIVE/DCIM"; the AI calls tools:run for tool:list-a-drive-folder with path (and offset and limit for a long folder).
3. Read entries (folders first, then files with numbers in natural order, hidden names left out) and total; when has_more is true, ask again with offset set to the entries you have seen.
4. A path off the connected drives, or a symbolic link that leaves the drive, is refused with "not on a connected drive".

worked_examples.title: Look inside the DCIM folder of a drive
worked_examples.ask: List the files in the DCIM folder on my SAMPLE DRIVE.
worked_examples.given: From tools/connected-drives/test/drives.test.mjs (lists one folder on a drive): DCIM holds a folder Day 2, clip-9.mov (1 byte), clip-10.mov (2 bytes) and a hidden file .hidden. The test runs on a pretend drive; the path here is the same shape on a real mount.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"path":"/Volumes/SAMPLE DRIVE/DCIM","name":"DCIM","mount":"/Volumes/SAMPLE DRIVE","entries":[{"name":"Day 2","kind":"folder","bytes":null},{"name":"clip-9.mov","kind":"file","file_kind":"video","bytes":1},{"name":"clip-10.mov","kind":"file","file_kind":"video","bytes":2}],"total":3,"has_more":false} (each entry also has its full path and modified_at; the hidden file is left out, and clip-9 comes before clip-10).
